q: How much fuel does automatic temperature control on a zinc bath save?
title: Zinc bath temperature control: oil saved
short: Holding a Howrah zinc bath at 500 °C instead of 520 °C with an automatic controller saves 4,442 litres of furnace oil a year in BEE's study, 3.8% of the furnace's 118,080 litres. That is 13.2 t CO2, not the report's 15 t. Cost Rs 2.34 lakh; payback 1.8 years at Rs 30 a litre.
audience: Hot-dip galvanizers in Howrah and elsewhere firing zinc kettles on furnace oil

p: IS 2629:1985 suggests a zinc bath of 440 to 460 °C. Howrah units run 480 to 520 °C to keep output up and help the centrifuge shed excess zinc, and operators keep it high to be safe when job sizes change. BEE found 490 to 500 °C, held steady, enough for production. A hotter bath burns more oil and makes more dross and ash, so zinc is lost too.

ul: A thermocouple in the bath and a temperature controller.
A VFD panel on the 0.37 kW fuel pump and the 15 kW blower, so the firing rate follows bath temperature.
Air control is a separate project in BEE's series; this one sets the fuel rate only.
Cost: Rs 2.25 lakh for the system plus Rs 0.09 lakh other, Rs 2.34 lakh.

sections.h: How the 4,442 litres was worked out
p: The unit galvanizes 2,399 t a year: 2,229 t of steel and 170 t of zinc. Heating that metal to 500 °C instead of 520 °C takes 5.13 million kcal less a year. Divided by the furnace's low efficiency, about 12%, that is 4,442 litres of oil, 3.8% of what it burns.

ul: Money: 4,442 x Rs 30 = Rs 1,33,260; Rs 2.34 lakh pays back in 1.76 years. At your oil price, the saving is 4,442 times the price per litre.
CO2: it claims 15 t at 3.24 t per tonne of oil, but 4,442 litres is 4,087 kg, and even its own factor gives 13.2 t. At 2.97 kg per litre it is also 13.2 t.

ol: Furnace oil per tonne galvanized, month by month.
Zinc bought per tonne galvanized, which should fall as dross falls.

example.title: One furnace, one year
lines: Oil saved: 4,442 L x 2.97 = 13.2 t CO2
Oil before: 118,080 L x 2.97 = 350.7 t CO2
Money at Rs 30 a litre: Rs 1,33,260; at Rs 60, Rs 2,66,520 and under a year to pay back
example.note: Furnace oil at 2.97 kg CO2 per litre. Oil price is the report's; use your own invoice price.

senseible: Senseible reads furnace oil invoices into monthly records at 2.97 kg CO2 per litre; add tonnes galvanized and the drop in oil per tonne shows month by month. The calculators give a quick CO2 figure.
